profile.behavior: A strongly migratory, vocal, colonial tern with buoyant rowing flight; forages singly or in flocks by picking prey from the surface or plunge-diving for small fish, and vigorously defends its nesting territory.
field_marks: Full black breeding cap surrounding a dark eye
Slender, straight orange-red bill, usually with a black tip
Pale gray upperparts and white to very light gray underparts
Long, narrow, pointed wings with darker outer primaries
Deeply forked tail with elongated outer feathers
profile.habitat: Breeds colonially on rocky islands, barrier beaches, saltmarshes, and sparsely vegetated sand, gravel, shell, or cobble near water. Forages over coastal waters, estuaries, inlets, and large inland lakes; chiefly marine outside the breeding season.

findings: The plate depicts one complete primary adult Common Tern with one head and bill, two folded wings, two short legs with webbed feet, and one deeply forked tail; the detached wing and head are clearly supplementary studies.

Adult plumage agrees with the references and direct sources: full black cap, dark eye, slender red-orange black-tipped bill, pale-gray body, dark outer primaries, red-orange legs, pointed wings, and elongated outer tail feathers.

Bill proportions are consistent between both depicted heads and the clearest side-profile reference: the upper mandible projects slightly beyond the lower without truncation, reversal, or exaggerated mismatch.
The primary specimen is somewhat fuller-bodied than the photographed adults, but remains within plausible posture and feathering variation and retains diagnostic Common Tern proportions.
Common name, scientific name, and family are correct. eBird independently identifies Common Tern as Sterna hirundo in Laridae.

All visible measurement text is accurate against the Cornell source: length 31–38 cm, weight 93–200 g, and wingspan 75–80 cm. Audubon publishes a different but overlapping measurement set, so the displayed Cornell ranges are supported rather than universal.
All habitat, behavior, field-mark, and palette text is complete, correctly spelled, coherent, and matches the proposed wording without omissions, substitutions, or duplicated words.

The body-length ruler is internally consistent: 31 cm is at the bottom, 38 cm at the top, four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks divide the range into five proportional segments, and the diagram is explicitly labeled schematic and not to scale.
